entry.summary: Buy a tourist card at the airport for up to 90 days.
entry.other: Central American Border Control Agreement (CA-4): one 90-day period covers land travel between Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The official currency is the US Dollar ($US). Exchange for other currencies isn't available. Bitcoin became legal tender in El Salvador in September 2021. However, not all vendors accept Bitcoin and it is in the early stages of adoption. Credit cards aren't widely accepted outside major centres. ATMs aren't reliable. Only change money and use ATMs in banks, hotels or shopping malls (see 'Safety').

consular.mission: Australian Consulate, San Salvador; Australian Embassy, Mexico City
consular.notes: Australia has a consulate in San Salvador, headed by an Honorary Consul. The consulate provides limited consular assistance to Australians in El Salvador. The Consulate can conduct passport interviews and provide provisional travel documents for emergency travel to the nearest Australian embassy. The Consulate can’t issue Australian passports. laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and include long prison sentences in local jails. Authorities will arrest you for illegal drugs if you're either: carrying even a very small amount of drugs, or with someone who's using them If you're found driving under the influence of alcohol or other drugs, authorities will arrest you. Border officials may screen you for drugs, including on departure. - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Public displays of affection may attract negative attention. Same-sex relationships are legal in El Salvador, but the country is conservative. Same-sex marriages are recognised in El Salvador.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: If you injure or kill someone in a road accident, authorities may arrest or detain you for a local trial. It's illegal to take photographs of official buildings. Check with local authorities before taking photos.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: To drive a vehicle, you'll need a current Australian driver's licence (digital driver’s licences may not be accepted).
laws.heading: Driving permit

conditional: Yellow fever vaccination certificate depending on where you've travelled from or through
health-entry.notes: Depending on where you've travelled, you may need a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter El Salvador. Some airlines may want to see one when you leave. Australia asks for a yellow fever certificate when you return from a country with yellow fever risk.
